Billets are semi-finished steel products; imports are typically from Russia, Ukraine, or Southeast Asia to supplement domestic steel supply during capacity shortfalls.
rics.how_to_use: China is the world's largest steel producer (~55% of global output); billet imports are typically small and signal domestic supply tightness. Billet imports surge when domestic capacity is curtailed (e.g., winter production restrictions, environmental crackdowns). Track alongside Chinese crude steel output from NBS.

rics.subcategory: Billet & Rough Forgings Imports — Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's billet and rough forgings imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. May reflect a different HS classification capturing hot-rolled billets vs. continuous cast or specific forging grades.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNCNRBIYM to construct a comprehensive picture of semi-finished steel import flows. Rough forgings imports track heavy equipment, power generation, and shipbuilding demand for large steel components. Post-Ukraine war, Russian billet supplies to China rose as EU/US doors closed.

rics.description: Import, billets & rough forgings, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Billets & Rough Forgings Imports — Value Series A
rics.meaning: Monthly current-price value series for China's billets and rough forgings imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Provides the value dimension for tracking semi-finished steel trade flows alongside volume metrics.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with volume data (aCNCNKKDTM) to derive implied import price per tonne; compare to international steel billet benchmarks (Black Sea export billet, CFR East Asia). Price premium vs international benchmarks indicates domestic tightness; discount signals oversupply or quality differences.

rics.description: Import, billets & rough forgings, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Billets & Rough Forgings Imports — Value Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate current-price value series for China's billets and rough forgings imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Multiple value series across billet categories reflect breadth of HS classifications for semi-finished ferrous products.
rics.how_to_use: Use together with aCNCNCEZGM for redundancy checking on billet value flows. Track the US-China steel tariff (Section 232) and any retaliatory measures' effects — Chinese steel exports have been subject to global trade remedies, affecting domestic production incentives and import levels.

rics.description: Import, billets & rough forgings, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's billets and rough forgings imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data captures the physical steel semi-fabricate flow independent of price movements.
rics.how_to_use: Volume data provides the clearest signal of physical semi-finished steel demand. Compare against NBS domestic steel production and inventory data. During steel supply-restriction periods (winter 2017-18, blue-sky policy 2018), billet import volumes spiked. Track Russian and Southeast Asian origin share post-2022.

rics.description: Import, caprolactam, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's caprolactam imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Caprolactam is the monomer for Nylon-6 production; China imports it from Japan, South Korea, and Europe to feed its large synthetic fiber and engineering plastics industries.
rics.how_to_use: Caprolactam imports track nylon supply-chain health. Rising imports signal expansion of China's nylon-6 fiber and resin production. Pair with polyamide fiber imports (aCNCNKUNLM) to understand the full nylon supply picture. Petrochemical feedstock (cyclohexane) price cycles drive caprolactam import cost.

rics.description: Import, caprolactam, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's caprolactam imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNHOPOM for validation; differences may reflect different HS sub-codes.
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate aCNCNHOPOM and this series for total caprolactam import value. China's domestic caprolactam production has expanded rapidly; the import vs domestic production balance tracks the degree of import substitution. Major suppliers: BASF (Germany), Sumitomo (Japan), DSM (Netherlands).

rics.description: Import, caprolactam, Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's caprolactam imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data strips out price volatility to reveal true physical demand for this nylon-6 precursor chemical.
rics.how_to_use: Compute unit value (value/volume) against Asian caprolactam spot prices to validate data quality. Volume trends of ~500-800K tonnes annually. Domestic Chinese caprolactam capacity expansions (several large plants in 2018-2022) should trend volume lower over time as import substitution occurs.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's cassava imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China imports cassava (tapioca chips/starch) primarily from Thailand and Vietnam for use as an animal feed starch source and ethanol feedstock.
rics.how_to_use: Cassava imports compete with corn and sorghum in China's animal feed supply balance. When corn prices are elevated (due to domestic production shortfall or policy), cassava imports rise as a substitute feed energy source. Track alongside corn futures (CBOT or Dalian) to monitor substitution dynamics.

rics.meaning: Alternate series for China's cassava imports, likely volume-based. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Thailand is China's dominant cassava supplier (~80% share); Vietnam supplies most of the remainder.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with value series (aCNCNKHQOM) to assess unit price. China imports ~5-8 million tonnes/year of cassava chips; volumes spike during corn shortages. This is also a useful proxy for Thai agricultural export competitiveness and Thai-China trade relations.

rics.description: Import, chrome ore & its concentrates, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's chrome ore and concentrate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Chrome ore is essential for stainless steel production; China has minimal domestic chrome reserves and imports almost entirely from South Africa, Kazakhstan, and India.
rics.how_to_use: Chrome ore imports directly track Chinese stainless steel production volumes — ~50% of global stainless is produced in China. Rising imports signal stainless mill restocking or production expansion. South Africa provides ~75% of global chromite exports. Compare against stainless steel output data for inventory-build versus consumption signals.

rics.description: Import, chrome ore & its concentrates, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's chrome ore and concentrate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data captures physical ore demand independent of price; critical for tracking Chinese stainless steel supply-chain requirements.
rics.how_to_use: China imports ~15-18 million tonnes of chrome ore per year. Volume surges indicate stainless mill restocking ahead of production ramp-ups. Compare with NBS stainless steel output — each tonne of stainless steel requires ~0.5 tonnes of chromite ore (Cr2O3 basis). Supply concentration risk: South Africa alone provides majority.

rics.subcategory: Chromium Ore & Concentrate Imports — Series A
rics.meaning: Monthly value series for China's chromium ore imports, potentially covering a different HS classification than aCNCNASAFM (e.g., beneficiated vs. run-of-mine ore). Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNCNASAFM and aCNCNKNVSM for cross-validation. Higher-grade chrome ore (>46% Cr2O3) commands premium pricing and is used directly in ferrochrome production. Track ferrochrome producer margins — when ferrochrome prices are strong, Chinese mills increase ore procurement.

rics.subcategory: Chromium Ore & Concentrate Imports — Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate series for China's chromium ore and concentrate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. May capture volume data for a sub-category of chromite ore not covered in aCNCNQZWIM.
rics.how_to_use: Integrate across chromium ore series for comprehensive stainless steel raw material tracking. China's chromium ore import dependency (100%) means supply disruptions from South Africa (power outages, port congestion) immediately impact stainless production. Track port stock data alongside monthly imports.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machine tools. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. CNC machine tools are critical capital goods for precision manufacturing; China imports high-end CNC equipment from Japan, Germany, and Switzerland.
rics.how_to_use: CNC machine tool imports are a leading indicator of Chinese manufacturing investment. Rising imports signal capex expansion cycles in automotive, aerospace, and electronics manufacturing. US export controls (Entity List) restrict some advanced CNC technology exports to China; track for supply diversification to Japan and EU. Pair with FAI data.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's total coal and lignite imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is the world's largest coal importer (~300-500 million tonnes/year); key suppliers are Australia, Indonesia, Russia, Mongolia, and the US.
rics.how_to_use: THE headline coal import series. Compare against domestic coal production (NBS) for the production-vs-import balance. Post-2022 Russian coal surge (replacing Australian coal, which was banned 2020-2023). Watch for seasonal restocking ahead of winter heating demand and summer air-conditioning peak. Monitor for SRB strategic stockpiling activity.

rics.description: Import, coking bituminous coal, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Coking Bituminous Coal Imports — Value Series A
rics.meaning: Monthly current-price value of China's coking bituminous coal imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Coking coal is the metallurgical grade coal used to make coke for blast furnace steelmaking; Australia historically supplies ~60% of China's coking coal imports.
rics.how_to_use: Coking coal imports directly track Chinese steel production via blast furnace route. Compare against spot coking coal prices (Australian premium hard coking coal FOB) to assess volume vs price effects. Post-2020 Australia coal ban sharply diverted flows to Russia, Mongolia, and Canada. Watch for ban reversal effects (Australia ban lifted May 2023).

rics.description: Import, coking bituminous coal, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Coking Bituminous Coal Imports — Value Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate current-price value series for China's coking bituminous coal imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-validate with aCNCNRDOIM to confirm coking coal import values.
rics.how_to_use: Multiple coking coal series may reflect different grades (premium hard vs semi-hard/semi-soft coking coal) or port-of-entry reporting. Pair value with volume (aCNCNKXVM) to derive unit import price; compare to Platts Premium Coking Coal Price Assessment for quality-grade verification.

rics.description: Import, coking bituminous coal, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Coking Bituminous Coal Imports — Value Series C
rics.meaning: Third current-price value series for China's coking bituminous coal imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. The multiplicity of series reflects different HS code sub-classifications within bituminous coal.
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate across aCNCNRDOIM, aCNCNVQAM, and this series for total coking coal import value exposure. The 2020-2023 Australian ban provides a natural experiment in trade diversion; Russian and Mongolian coking coal dramatically increased share. This transition matters for quality (Australian coking coal is higher quality).

rics.description: Import, coking bituminous coal, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's coking bituminous coal imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data separates physical supply from price effects; China imports ~70-90 million tonnes of coking coal annually for its ~1 billion tonne per year steel industry.
rics.how_to_use: Divide by blast furnace steel output (approximately 0.7 tonnes coking coal per tonne of pig iron) to validate import volumes against production. Volume drops during Australian ban (2020-2023) confirmed diversification to Russia/Mongolia. Ban lift in 2023 saw Australian volumes recover; watch for market share dynamics.

rics.description: Import, coking bituminous coal, Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Coking Bituminous Coal Imports — Volume Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly volume series for China's coking bituminous coal imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNQDYTM for volume reconciliation across HS code categories.
rics.how_to_use: Reconcile with aCNCNQDYTM to confirm total coking coal import volumes. Geographic decomposition (Australia, Russia, Mongolia, Canada) is available via country-specific series. Track Qinhuangdao port coal stocks alongside import volumes for the supply-chain inventory picture.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's copper imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China consumes ~55% of global refined copper (~12 million tonnes/year); major import sources are Chile, Peru, Australia, and DRC for concentrate, and refined copper from various sources.
rics.how_to_use: One of the most globally-watched Chinese commodity import series. Decompose: copper concentrate imports (feed for domestic smelters) vs refined copper imports (direct consumption). Copper demand tracks Chinese infrastructure investment, property sector, and renewable energy (EVs, solar, wind require 3-6x more copper than conventional). SRB stockpiling also drives swings.

rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's copper imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. May capture a different form of copper (wire rod, fabricated products, scrap copper) versus primary concentrate/refined in aCNCNRYABM.
rics.how_to_use: If this series tracks copper scrap, compare to refined copper imports for substitution dynamics. China's 2019 scrap import restrictions (National Sword) reshaped global copper scrap flows. Track combined refined + scrap copper imports against SHFE copper price and LME-SHFE spread for arbitrage signals.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's corrugated paper imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Corrugated paper (containerboard) is the primary packaging material for e-commerce and consumer goods; China imports specialty grades from the US, Europe, and Japan.
rics.how_to_use: China's paper industry has rapidly expanded domestic capacity; corrugated paper imports are relatively small. Rising imports signal domestic capacity constraints or demand for specialty quality grades. Track alongside e-commerce volume growth (JD, Alibaba GMV) as a packaging demand proxy. US waste paper exports to China were curtailed by 2018 import restrictions.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's cotton woven fabric imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China imports specialized cotton fabrics from Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, and Turkey for garment manufacturing, despite being a large domestic cotton and textile producer.
rics.how_to_use: Cotton fabric imports reflect quality differentiation — imports tend to be finer count fabrics. Compare against domestic cotton yarn output (NBS) and Xinjiang cotton production to assess upstream supply. US sanctions on Xinjiang cotton (UFLPA 2022) can redirect Chinese fabric sourcing toward other origins.

rics.description: Import, current, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly current-price import value series, covering a broad or residual import category. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. The generic label suggests this may be a totals or cross-category aggregate series.
rics.how_to_use: Identify which commodity or trade category this series represents by cross-referencing against known HS codes and total import aggregates. If confirmed as an aggregate, compare with headline import figures (aCNCIMPB/A) and the YoY change (aCNIMPGDA) for consistency checks.

rics.description: Import, current, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Alternate current-price import value series. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Likely represents a second HS classification range or product group within broader import categories.
rics.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNCNZTDMM and aCNCNYEJOM to triangulate total or sub-category import values. If these three series together form an aggregated import value, sum them and compare to aCNCIMPB/A to verify completeness.

rics.description: Import, current, Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume series associated with the current import categories. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data provides the physical flow dimension to complement the value series.
rics.how_to_use: Compute unit import price (aCNCNZTDMM or aCNCNBWPLM divided by this volume series) to derive implicit import deflator. Compare deflator to relevant commodity price indices (PPI, CRB) to assess data quality and price-vs-volume decomposition.

rics.description: Import, diesel oil, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's diesel oil imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is both a major diesel producer and occasionally an importer during domestic supply shortfalls; import volumes are typically small relative to domestic production.
rics.how_to_use: Diesel imports are countercyclical to domestic refinery utilization — they rise during refinery maintenance seasons or when domestic diesel demand peaks sharply (agricultural harvest season, winter heating transport). Compare against domestic diesel production (NBS) and commercial vehicle sales data.

rics.description: Import, diesel oil, Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's diesel oil imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data is essential to distinguish physical diesel supply shortfalls from price-driven value changes.
rics.how_to_use: China typically exports more diesel than it imports; a reversal to net import status is a meaningful supply signal. Monitor against domestic refinery utilization rates (Sinopec, PetroChina data) and national diesel inventory levels. EV penetration in commercial trucks is reducing diesel import dependency over time.

rics.description: Import, digital program-controlled telephone or telegraph switch, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Digital Program-Controlled Telecom Switch Imports — Value A
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of digital program-controlled telephone and telegraph switches. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Reflects imports of telecom network switching equipment from global suppliers including Cisco, Nokia, and Ericsson.
rics.how_to_use: Telecom switch imports reflect 5G network buildout spending and legacy 4G infrastructure upgrades. Falling imports may signal Huawei domestic substitution success — Huawei, ZTE increasingly supply domestic telecoms capex. US Entity List restrictions on US equipment exports to China influence import-source diversification.

rics.description: Import, digital program-controlled telephone or telegraph switch, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Digital Program-Controlled Telecom Switch Imports — Value B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's digital program-controlled telecom switch imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. May cover a different telecom equipment sub-category or reporting vintage.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNCNAACM for total telecom switch import value. The secular decline in this category since 2015 reflects the rapid maturation of domestic Chinese telecom equipment manufacturers (Huawei, ZTE, FiberHome). Rising series would signal either a technology gap or preferential foreign procurement.

rics.description: Import, fishmealfor feed, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Fishmeal for Feed Imports — Value A
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's fishmeal imports for animal feed. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Fishmeal is a high-protein feed ingredient for aquaculture, hog, and poultry production; China imports primarily from Peru and Chile.
rics.how_to_use: Fishmeal imports track Chinese aquaculture intensity and protein feed demand. Peru's anchovy catch (El Nino sensitive) dominates global fishmeal supply; El Nino-driven shortfalls drive price spikes. Compare against soybean meal imports (aCNCNMVIOM) to assess substitution between plant and marine protein in Chinese feed.

rics.description: Import, fishmealfor feed, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Fishmeal for Feed Imports — Value B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's fishmeal imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNBBQOM to validate total fishmeal import value.
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate aCNCNBBQOM and this series for complete fishmeal import value. Fishmeal price is highly seasonal (Peruvian fishing seasons: April-June and November-January). During fishing bans or El Nino events, fishmeal prices surge and Chinese buyers may substitute with blood meal, feather meal, or soybean meal.

rics.description: Import, fishmealfor feed, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's fishmeal imports for feed. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data separates physical fishmeal procurement from price fluctuations, which are substantial given supply volatility.
rics.how_to_use: China imports ~1.5-2 million tonnes of fishmeal per year. Volume surges in Q1 and Q3 reflect Peruvian fishing season timing. Pair volume with value (aCNCNBBQOM) to compute unit price and compare with global fishmeal benchmarks (Hamburg, Peru FOB). Compare with aquaculture production data for demand-driven analysis.

rics.description: Import, frozen chicken, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's frozen chicken imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is a major chicken importer, sourcing from Brazil and US (when not under trade restrictions), for food service, processed meat, and processed food industries.
rics.how_to_use: Frozen chicken imports track Chinese protein consumption cycles. Demand surges post-African Swine Fever (2019-2021) when pork prices spiked, driving substitution into poultry. Brazil dominates (70%+ of Chinese frozen chicken imports). Compare against domestic poultry production (NBS) to assess import dependency.

rics.description: Import, frozen chicken, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's frozen chicken imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. May capture a sub-category (e.g., chicken parts vs. whole chicken) or different trade reporting vintage.
rics.how_to_use: China primarily imports chicken paws, wings, and leg quarters — parts less consumed in supplier countries. Brazilian origin dominates. Cross-reference aCNCNVHISM for consistency. Track US chicken import access (subject to periodic bans due to bird flu) as US chicken paw exports are significant when permitted.

rics.description: Import, frozen chicken, Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's frozen chicken imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data tracks the physical quantity of imported poultry, separating demand signals from frozen chicken price fluctuations.
rics.how_to_use: China imports ~400-600K tonnes of frozen chicken annually; volumes surged 50%+ during ASF period (2019-2020). Pair with value data (aCNCNVHISM) to compute unit price. Rising volumes with falling unit prices signal Chinese buyers are seeking cheaper protein substitutes during pork supply shortfalls.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's heavy fuel oil (No. 5-7, residual fuel) imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Heavy fuel oil is used in power generation, maritime shipping bunkers, and industrial heating; China imports from Russia, Singapore, and Middle East.
rics.how_to_use: Heavy fuel oil imports signal power sector stress — imports surge when domestic coal supply is tight (e.g., 2021 power crisis). Maritime bunker demand in Chinese ports (Shanghai, Ningbo) also drives imports. Post-IMO 2020 (low sulphur shipping fuel rules), watch for shifts between fuel oil grades.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's gasoline imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is generally a net exporter of gasoline given its large refinery fleet; imports occur during refinery shutdowns or domestic supply shortfalls.
rics.how_to_use: Gasoline imports are atypical for China; their presence signals domestic supply gaps. Compare against domestic gasoline production (NBS refinery output) and commercial gasoline demand proxy (passenger car sales). Rising EV penetration is structurally reducing gasoline demand growth; track against NEV sales data.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of generator sets and rotary converters. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Generator imports reflect demand for backup power, industrial power applications, and specialized power electronics from Germany, Japan, and the US.
rics.how_to_use: Generator set imports track industrial investment cycles and power reliability concerns. Surges may signal elevated power-grid stress (prompting backup power purchases) or industrial park construction. Compare with fixed asset investment (FAI) data; large generator sets are key capital goods for manufacturing facilities.

rics.description: Import, isocyanate, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's isocyanate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Isocyanates (MDI, TDI) are core polyurethane feedstocks used in rigid foam insulation, flexible foam (mattresses, automotive seating), adhesives, and coatings.
rics.how_to_use: Isocyanate imports track Chinese polyurethane industry growth. MDI imports from BASF and Covestro (Germany) and Wanhua Chemical (China now dominates domestically). Rising imports signal domestic MDI/TDI production insufficient for demand. Property sector insulation demand drives rigid foam MDI cycles.

rics.description: Import, isocyanate, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's isocyanate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. May cover TDI (toluene diisocyanate) versus MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) sub-categories.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNCNWRNM. China's Wanhua Chemical became a global MDI leader (~30% of world capacity); the degree to which China still needs to import MDI vs TDI varies. TDI remains more import-dependent. Track Wanhua MDI spot prices vs import price as an arbitrage indicator.

rics.description: Import, isocyanate, Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's isocyanate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data reveals physical demand for polyurethane precursors independent of isocyanate price swings, which can be substantial.
rics.how_to_use: China imports ~200-400K tonnes/year of isocyanates depending on domestic capacity utilization. Pair with value (aCNCNWRNM) to compute unit price versus Asian isocyanate spot markets. Monitor Wanhua Chemical's domestic capacity additions — each new MDI train reduces import dependency by ~200K tonnes/year.

rics.description: Import, kerosene, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's kerosene (jet fuel / aviation turbine fuel) imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Kerosene imports track Chinese aviation demand and domestic jet fuel supply adequacy.
rics.how_to_use: Kerosene imports are a proxy for aviation demand when domestic refinery capacity cannot meet jet fuel demand. Post-COVID recovery in international flights (2023-2024) drove kerosene demand recovery. Track alongside Chinese civil aviation passenger volume data (CAAC) and domestic refinery jet fuel production (NBS).

rics.description: Import, kerosene, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's kerosene imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNZPUYM for kerosene import validation across HS classifications.
rics.how_to_use: Compare aCNCNZPUYM and this series for total kerosene import coverage. Singapore and South Korea are the primary suppliers of imported jet fuel to China. Track domestic aviation routes expansion and Airbus/Boeing delivery schedules for medium-term jet fuel demand drivers.

rics.description: Import, kerosene, Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's kerosene imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data strips jet fuel price volatility to show physical supply import demand.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with value series (aCNCNZPUYM) to compute unit jet fuel price; compare to Singapore jet fuel price benchmarks (MOPS Jet A1). China is typically a net jet fuel exporter; import volume surges signal acute demand-supply imbalance. Monitor CAAC monthly passenger-kilometers for demand context.

rics.description: Import, kraft paper, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Kraft Paper Imports — Value Series A
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's kraft paper imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Kraft paper is used for packaging, bags, and as liner material in corrugated board; China imports from Sweden, Finland, Brazil, and Canada where high-quality wood pulp supports premium kraft production.
rics.how_to_use: Kraft paper imports track packaging demand and domestic paper mill capacity limits. China's packaging industry growth (e-commerce) has driven demand; domestic capacity expansion is reducing imports. Compare with domestic paper production data and wood pulp imports (related input) for supply-chain completeness.

rics.description: Import, kraft paper, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Kraft Paper Imports — Value Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's kraft paper imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-validate with aCNCNYOPXM for total kraft paper import value.
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate with aCNCNYOPXM for comprehensive kraft paper import value. Falling kraft paper imports over time indicate successful domestic substitution. Track Nordic paper exports (Finland, Sweden) to China as the primary premium-quality source. Compare kraft paper import prices against domestic Chinese paper prices for arbitrage signals.

rics.description: Import, kraft paper, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's kraft paper imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data tracks physical paper import procurement independent of international pulp and paper price cycles.
rics.how_to_use: Compare volume against value (aCNCNYOPXM) to derive unit import price; benchmark against international kraft paper price indices (FOEX, RISI). China imports ~500K-1 million tonnes of kraft paper/year; volumes trend downward as domestic capacity expands. Monitor for demand-driven spikes tied to e-commerce packaging demand.

rics.subcategory: Lead Ore & Concentrate Imports — Series A
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's lead ore and concentrate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is the world's largest lead producer and consumer (~50% of global demand); lead ore imports supplement domestic mine output for battery manufacturing.
rics.how_to_use: Lead demand in China is overwhelmingly driven by lead-acid batteries (automotive, e-bikes, UPS). Import volumes track smelter utilization and domestic mine depletion. Australia and Peru are major ore suppliers. Compare against SHFE lead prices and LME spreads for arbitrage incentives. Secondary lead (recycling) competes with ore imports.

rics.subcategory: Lead Ore & Concentrate Imports — Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's lead ore and concentrate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-validate with aCNCNREDGM for total lead ore import value.
rics.how_to_use: Lead imports link directly to Chinese e-bike and automotive battery production cycles. China has ~350 million e-bikes, almost all lead-acid battery powered; replacement cycle (~3 years) creates stable base demand. Monitor for lithium-ion substitution in e-bikes which would erode lead demand structurally.

rics.subcategory: Lead Ore & Concentrate Imports — Series C
rics.meaning: Third series for China's lead ore and concentrate imports, likely volume-based. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data provides the physical procurement dimension for lead ore supply-chain analysis.
rics.how_to_use: Compute unit import price from value/volume; benchmark against LME lead price minus refining charges. China's domestic lead mines (Henan, Yunnan) supply majority of needs; imports supplement. Smelter margins (treatment charges TC/RC) determine whether Chinese smelters prefer domestic vs imported concentrate.

rics.description: Import, linear low density polyethylene in primary form
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) in primary form. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. LLDPE is used in stretch film, agricultural mulch film, food packaging, and cable insulation; China imports from Saudi Arabia, Middle East, and US.
rics.how_to_use: LLDPE imports track agricultural plastics demand (mulch film for vegetable/fruit production is massive in China) and packaging film demand. Domestic ethylene cracker expansions reduce import dependency over time. Track ethylene feedstock pricing vs naphtha to understand Middle East cost advantage for LLDPE exports to China.

rics.description: Import, machinery & parts for manufacture of paper & paper products
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of machinery for manufacturing paper and paper products. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is expanding its domestic paper industry; large paper machines are imported from Germany (Voith, Andritz) and Finland.
rics.how_to_use: Paper machinery imports are a leading indicator of Chinese paper industry capex cycles. Surges precede new paper machine startups 2-4 years later, signaling future domestic paper production capacity additions. Monitor against Chinese paper imports (aCNCNYOPXM) — rising machinery imports implies rising future domestic output and lower paper imports.

rics.description: Import, manganese ore & its concentrate, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Manganese Ore & Concentrate Imports — Value A
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's manganese ore and concentrate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Manganese is essential for steel production (desulfurization) and lithium-ion battery cathodes; China imports primarily from South Africa, Gabon, Australia, and Ghana.
rics.how_to_use: Manganese ore imports track steel production indirectly (each tonne of steel requires ~7kg of manganese) and increasingly battery cathode production (NMC batteries). South Africa's Kalahari Manganese Field is the world's largest reserve; port and rail disruptions there affect Chinese imports. EV battery demand creates structural growth.

rics.description: Import, manganese ore & its concentrate, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Manganese Ore & Concentrate Imports — Value B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's manganese ore imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNXJGRM for total manganese ore value validation.
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate with aCNCNXJGRM for total manganese import value. Gabon (COMILOG mine) is a key alternative to South African supply; trade route diversification matters for supply security. Rising manganese import value tracks both steel industry capex (alloy steel) and battery supply chain (high-purity manganese for LMFP cathodes).

rics.description: Import, manganese ore & its concentrate, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Manganese Ore & Concentrate Imports — Volume A
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's manganese ore and concentrate imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data separates physical demand from price effects; critical for steel production and battery cathode supply-chain analysis.
rics.how_to_use: China imports ~20-25 million tonnes of manganese ore per year. Compute unit price from value/volume; benchmark against CRU or Platts manganese ore price index (37% Mn, CIF Tianjin). Volume surges ahead of steel mill restocking; battery-grade high-purity manganese imports may track separately at higher unit values.

rics.description: Import, manganese ore & its concentrate, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Manganese Ore & Concentrate Imports — Volume B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly volume series for China's manganese ore imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNHXUM for volume reconciliation.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNCNHXUM for comprehensive manganese import volume coverage. Track Australian Groote Eylandt Mining (GEMCO) production — a major Chinese supplier — for supply disruption signals. Manganese ore supply-demand is tighter than many base metals; inventory cycles can be sharp.

rics.description: Import, manmade fiber staple fiber, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Manmade Fiber Staple Fiber Imports — Value A
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's manmade staple fiber imports (polyester, viscose, nylon, acrylic). Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is the world's largest textile producer; specialty manmade staple fibers are imported from Taiwan, South Korea, and India.
rics.how_to_use: Manmade staple fiber imports track the higher-value, specialty-grade segment of textile inputs. Domestic Chinese production dominates commodity grades (polyester PSF); imports tend to be specialty viscose, modal, or technical fibers. Compare against domestic staple fiber output (NBS) to assess import dependency by fiber type.

rics.description: Import, manmade fiber staple fiber, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Manmade Fiber Staple Fiber Imports — Value B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's manmade fiber staple fiber imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNQFVQM for total staple fiber import value.
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate with aCNCNQFVQM for total manmade staple fiber import value. The declining import trend reflects successful domestic substitution by Sinopec and Hengli Petrochemical expanding PTA/PET fiber capacity. Track PTA (purified terephthalic acid) import data alongside for polyester supply-chain coherence.

rics.description: Import, manmade fiber staple fiber, Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Manmade Fiber Staple Fiber Imports — Volume
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's manmade fiber staple fiber imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data provides the physical textile input flow independent of fiber price volatility.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with value data (aCNCNQFVQM) to derive unit fiber import price; compare to Asian polyester staple fiber price benchmarks. Volume trend downward reflects domestic capacity growth. Seasonal spikes in August-October (pre-winter apparel production) are typical. Monitor for viscose rayon import sub-category, dominated by Indian suppliers.

rics.subcategory: Metalworking Machine Tools Imports — Series A
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's metalworking machine tool imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Metalworking machine tools (lathes, milling machines, grinding machines) are critical capital goods; China imports high-precision equipment from Germany, Japan, and Switzerland.
rics.how_to_use: Machine tool imports are a key leading indicator of Chinese manufacturing investment. Germany (TRUMPF, DMG Mori), Japan (Fanuc, Mazak), and Switzerland (GF Machining, Tornos) dominate China's precision tool imports. US export controls on high-precision multi-axis machines affect import diversification. Pair with FAI manufacturing sub-component.

rics.subcategory: Metalworking Machine Tools Imports — Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's metalworking machine tool imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNNRZVM; may cover different HS sub-categories (e.g., laser cutting vs. CNC turning centers).
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate aCNCNNRZVM and this series for total machine tool import tracking. Machine tool imports peaked in the 2011-2015 manufacturing capex boom; current trend reflects maturation of Chinese domestic machine tool makers (Haas substitution, Shenyang Machine Tool recovery). Secular decline in imports indicates growing domestic capacity.

rics.description: Import, natural rubber (including latex), Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's natural rubber (including latex) imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is the world's largest natural rubber consumer (~35% of global supply); primary sources are Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Vietnam.
rics.how_to_use: Natural rubber imports track tire production (passenger and truck tires) which is China's dominant rubber end-use. Rising imports signal auto production growth and commercial vehicle fleet expansion. Compare against SHFE rubber futures and Thailand RSS3 prices to assess import cost dynamics. SRB stockpiling adds volatility in Q1.

rics.description: Import, natural rubber (including latex), Volume, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's natural rubber imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data strips out the significant rubber price volatility to reveal pure demand dynamics for this key manufacturing input.
rics.how_to_use: China imports ~5-6 million tonnes of natural rubber annually. Pair with value (aCNCNDMLNM) to compute unit price; compare to SICOM TSR20 benchmark. Volume surges in Q1 (pre-Lunar New Year stock building) and post-monsoon season (Thai harvest). EV tire demand (higher rubber content per tire) provides incremental demand growth.

rics.description: Import, non-foam plastic sheets, sheets, films & foils
rics.subcategory: Non-Foam Plastic Sheets, Films & Foils Imports
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of non-foam plastic sheets, films, and foils. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. This category includes technical films (BOPET, BOPP, optical film) imported from Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan for electronics, flexible packaging, and solar applications.
rics.how_to_use: Technical optical film imports (from Japan's Nitto Denko, Sumitomo Chemical) track LCD panel production cycles. BOPET and BOPP film imports track flexible packaging growth. Rising imports in optical-grade films signal electronics production expansion; compare against LCD panel output indices for validation.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's olive oil imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China has become a significant olive oil importer as middle-class dietary preferences shift toward Mediterranean cooking; Spain, Italy, and Greece are the primary suppliers.
rics.how_to_use: Olive oil imports are a proxy for Chinese premium consumer food spending and middle-class expansion. Rising imports track urbanization and disposable income growth. Compare with overall food import trends and luxury goods consumption data. Mediterranean drought/freeze events causing olive oil price spikes (2023-2024) are visible in this series.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of uncut paper and cardboard (rolls/sheets before cutting). Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China imports specialty printing and industrial grades from Finland, Sweden, and Japan.
rics.how_to_use: Uncut paper imports serve specialty printing, publishing, and industrial applications. Domestic Chinese paper mills increasingly produce commodity grades; specialty coated and supercalendered papers still require imports. Compare against domestic paper production output — import substitution has been rapid for commodity grades.

rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's uncut paper and cardboard imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-validate with aCNCNWPYM to confirm total paper and cardboard import values.
rics.how_to_use: Use with aCNCNWPYM for a comprehensive paper and cardboard import picture. The multi-year trend is declining imports as domestic Chinese paper capacity (Nine Dragons, Lee & Man) displaces foreign supply. Key data point: China went from large paper importer to net exporter by early 2020s for most grades.

rics.description: Import, passenger cars (including complete sets of spare parts)
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's passenger car imports (including CBU and CKD kits). Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China imports luxury and premium vehicles from Germany (BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche), US, and Japan; total ~800K-1M units annually.
rics.how_to_use: Passenger car imports track luxury/premium consumption sentiment. German brands dominate (~60% of import value). Compare against domestic luxury car sales (Jato Dynamics China data) to assess import vs local manufacture split. Trade tensions (US tariffs on cars, Chinese retaliatory tariffs) directly affect US brand import volumes. Tesla local production vs imports is key data point.

rics.description: Import, passenger cars (including complete sets of spare parts)
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's passenger car imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. May reflect a different categorization (e.g., CKD sets vs CBU, or specific engine displacement classes).
rics.how_to_use: Cross-reference with aCNCNTHIPM for total passenger car import picture. China's 25% import tariff on passenger cars (reduced to 15% under CPTPP for qualifying origins) is a key cost driver. Compare with wholesale registrations (CAAM data) to track import vs domestically manufactured vehicle market share dynamics.

rics.description: Import, peanut oil, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Peanut Oil Imports — Value Series A
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's peanut (groundnut) oil imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is both a major peanut producer and peanut oil importer; Senegal, Argentina, and Sudan are key import sources.
rics.how_to_use: Peanut oil imports reflect domestic supply gaps driven by peanut crop conditions in China (primarily Henan, Shandong). Rising imports signal domestic peanut harvest shortfall or demand outpacing production. Compare against soybean oil and palm oil imports for edible oil substitution dynamics.

rics.description: Import, peanut oil, Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Peanut Oil Imports — Value Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's peanut oil imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNEWRGM for total peanut oil import value.
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate with aCNCNEWRGM for comprehensive peanut oil import value. Peanut oil is premium-priced relative to soybean oil (~2x) and is used in traditional Chinese cooking; demand is income-elastic. Compare import volumes (aCNCNYYQTM, aCNCNDBHIM) for price decomposition against Qingdao peanut oil spot prices.

rics.description: Import, peanut oil, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Peanut Oil Imports — Volume Series A
rics.meaning: Monthly volume of China's peanut oil imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Volume data reveals physical peanut oil supply demand independent of edible oil price cycles.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with value (aCNCNEWRGM) to compute unit import price; compare to Chinese domestic peanut oil spot prices (Qingdao) and international benchmarks. Chinese peanut oil imports are ~100-300K tonnes/year — significantly smaller than soybean and palm oil imports. Cross-reference with aCNCNDBHIM for volume consistency.

rics.description: Import, peanut oil, Imports & Exports, Monthly, China Customs
rics.subcategory: Peanut Oil Imports — Volume Series B
rics.meaning: Alternate monthly volume series for China's peanut oil imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-validate with aCNCNYYQTM for total peanut oil import volumes.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNCNYYQTM for comprehensive peanut oil volume tracking. African suppliers (Senegal) are significant sources of crude peanut oil for Chinese refining. Supply seasonality (West African groundnut harvest: October-January) creates seasonal import patterns. Track COFCO and Wilmar Chinese edible oil procurement patterns.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's total pharmaceutical product imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China imports patented drugs, biologics, and innovative therapies from the US, Germany, Switzerland, and the UK for hospital and retail channels.
rics.how_to_use: Pharmaceutical imports track Chinese healthcare system development. Accelerated regulatory approvals (NMPA fast-track) and NRDL (National Reimbursement Drug List) inclusions drive import volumes. Post-COVID oncology drug imports surged. Compare against domestic generic drug production; rising imports with stable generics signals innovative drug demand growth.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's polyacrylonitrile (PAN/acrylic) fiber imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. PAN fiber is the precursor for carbon fiber; China imports both textile-grade acrylic fiber and PAN precursor for advanced composite materials.
rics.how_to_use: PAN fiber imports serve dual markets: commodity textile acrylic (sweaters, knitwear) and high-performance carbon fiber precursor. Carbon fiber PAN precursor imports are strategically sensitive — Japan (Toray, Teijin) dominates; US export controls complicate imports. Rising high-grade PAN imports signal aerospace/wind turbine composite expansion.

rics.meaning: Alternate series for China's polyacrylonitrile fiber imports, likely volume-based. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNNQKXM for total PAN fiber import data.
rics.how_to_use: Compute unit value from aCNCNNQKXM / this volume series to distinguish commodity acrylic (low unit value) from high-performance PAN precursor (high unit value ~$30-50/kg vs ~$3-5/kg). Rising unit values in this series indicate a shift toward high-performance carbon fiber precursor procurement.

rics.description: Import, polyamide fiber filaments (except sewing thread)
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's polyamide (nylon-6, nylon-66) fiber filament imports, excluding sewing thread. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Nylon filaments are used in hosiery, swimwear, activewear, airbags, and technical textiles; China imports specialty grades from Taiwan, South Korea, and Europe.
rics.how_to_use: Nylon filament imports track the specialty-performance apparel and technical textile sectors. Nylon-66 (used in airbags) faces supply constraints as Ascend and Invista dominate global supply. Compare against caprolactam imports (aCNCNHOPOM) — they compete as nylon-6 inputs vs. imported finished filament.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's polyester fiber imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Despite being the world's largest polyester producer (~70% of global capacity), China imports high-performance specialty polyester fibers from Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea.
rics.how_to_use: China's domestic polyester industry is massive; imports are specialty or premium-grade. High-tenacity industrial polyester (tyre cord, conveyor belts) and ultra-fine microfiber imports track technical textile demand. Compare against domestic PTA and MEG feedstock data — the full polyester supply chain is vertically integrated in China.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's pork imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is the world's largest pork consumer (~50% of global supply); import surges occurred during the African Swine Fever crisis (2018-2021) when domestic herd was decimated. Sources: EU, US, Brazil, Canada.
rics.how_to_use: THE headline meat import series. ASF-driven import surge (2019-2021) is the defining event — imports 3-4x'ed to ~3.8M tonnes. Post-herd-rebuild, imports normalized (2022-2024). Track domestic pig inventory (MARA data) and live hog prices (Zhuo Chuang) to forecast import need. US-China tariffs (2018+) pushed share to EU/Brazil.

rics.meaning: Alternate monthly series for China's pork imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Cross-reference with aCNCNQRZI for total pork import value; may reflect a different HS sub-category (frozen vs. chilled, bone-in vs. boneless, offals vs. muscle meat).
rics.how_to_use: China's pork import breakdown matters: offals (ears, feet, intestines) are imported at high volumes due to Chinese consumption preferences; muscle meat imports are more sensitive to price competition with domestic pork. EU typically wins on chilled fresh pork; Brazil on frozen cuts. Track China's MRL (maximum residue limit) policy changes for access restrictions.

rics.meaning: Current-period monthly value of China's pork imports, likely representing the most current or seasonally unadjusted series. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Directly comparable month-on-month for pork trade flow analysis.
rics.how_to_use: Use this current-period series for the most timely pork import signal. Monthly pork import data is keenly watched by global pork processors (Smithfield, JBS, Tyson) and commodity traders. Seasonal patterns: imports typically rise pre-Chinese New Year as processors stock up. Compare domestic hog-to-feed ratios to forecast import pull-through.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's potassium sulphate (SOP) imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. SOP is a premium potassium fertilizer used on chloride-sensitive crops (fruits, vegetables, tobacco); China imports from Germany (K+S), Chile (SQM), and Belgium.
rics.how_to_use: Potassium sulphate imports track specialty fertilizer demand for premium horticulture crops in China. Compare against muriate of potash (MOP/KCl) imports for potassium fertilizer substitution dynamics. SOP commands a ~3x premium to MOP; rising SOP imports signal quality upgrade in Chinese agricultural practices.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of PVC (polyvinyl chloride) in primary form. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. PVC is used in pipes, profiles, films, wire insulation, and flooring; China imports specialty grades from the US, Taiwan, and Japan.
rics.how_to_use: PVC imports track Chinese construction activity (PVC pipes, profiles for windows/doors account for ~50% of use) and property sector health. China is a large domestic PVC producer (calcium carbide route, acetylene route); imports are specialty grades. Property downturn (2021-2024) suppressed PVC imports. SRB strategic plastics stockpiling is minimal.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's polyester in primary form (PET resin) imports. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. PET resin is used for beverage bottles, food packaging, and textiles; China imports bottle-grade PET from Taiwan, South Korea, and Southeast Asia.
rics.how_to_use: PET resin imports track Chinese beverage industry growth and packaging demand. Compare domestic PET production (Hengli, Rongsheng) against import volumes for self-sufficiency assessment. Rising beverage consumption (sports drinks, water) and e-commerce food delivery packaging drive PET demand growth.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's polyethylene imports in primary form. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China imports polyethylene (HDPE, LDPE, LLDPE) from Saudi Arabia, US, South Korea, and Singapore for packaging, agriculture, and pipes.
rics.how_to_use: Polyethylene is China's largest volume plastic import category. Saudi Arabia and US (advantaged ethane feedstock) are low-cost suppliers. Rising imports signal domestic ethylene cracker capacity insufficient for demand. Agricultural film and packaging growth drives underlying demand. Track new Chinese coal-to-olefins projects for domestic supply additions.

rics.meaning: Alternate monthly value series for China's polyethylene imports in primary form. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. May cover a specific PE grade (HDPE vs LDPE) or different HS classification.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNCNZGXQM for total polyethylene import value. Differentiate by grade: HDPE (rigid packaging, pipes) vs LDPE (flexible packaging, agricultural film) vs LLDPE (stretch film). Middle East ethane-based producers hold ~25-30% cost advantage over Chinese naphtha crackers, driving structural import dependency.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's polypropylene imports in primary form. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. PP is used in packaging, automotive parts, textiles (non-wovens), and consumer goods; China imports specialty grades from South Korea, Japan, and Saudi Arabia.
rics.how_to_use: Polypropylene imports track Chinese auto production (interior parts, bumpers), packaging, and medical non-wovens demand. Domestic PP capacity (PDH plants) has expanded rapidly since 2018; import dependency declining. COVID-19 medical non-woven demand (masks, gowns) surged PP imports in 2020. Monitor domestic PDH utilization rates.

rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's styrene polymer imports in primary form (polystyrene, HIPS, EPS). Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Polystyrene is used in food packaging (EPS cups, containers), electronics (HIPS casings), and insulation; China imports from South Korea, Taiwan, and Singapore.
rics.how_to_use: Polystyrene imports track consumer electronics packaging, food service, and building insulation demand. EPS (expanded polystyrene) import volumes reflect cold chain packaging and construction insulation growth. Compare with ABS resin imports (aCNCNBKBMM) which share the styrene-based polymer space but serve different end markets.

rics.description: Import, pure electric cars & off-road vehicles
rics.meaning: Monthly value of China's imports of pure electric passenger cars and off-road vehicles. Published by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. Despite being the world's largest EV producer and market, China imports premium electric vehicles from Tesla (US), BMW, Mercedes-Benz EQ, and Volkswagen ID series.
rics.how_to_use: Electric vehicle imports are a fast-growing niche. Tesla's Shanghai Gigafactory has displaced most Tesla imports, but premium EV brands still import. Track against domestic NEV (new energy vehicle) production (CAAM data) to measure the import vs locally-manufactured premium EV split. US EV tariffs by China (retaliation) affect Tesla import volumes. Closely watch BYD's luxury brand EV launch to understand import substitution.

rics.how_to_use: Pro-cyclical with manufacturing + property investment cycles. Falls during property downturns. China imports YoY drop -10% in major slowdowns; +15% to +20% in commodity-cycle peaks.

rics.meaning: Merchandise Imports, level — total monthly goods imports. Major categories: integrated circuits, crude oil, iron ore, soybeans, machinery, copper.

rics.meaning: Merchandise Exports, level — total monthly goods exports. Released by China Customs ~7-10th of each month. China is the world's largest goods exporter (~$3.5T annually).
